title: Beware Escapism
coreMove: Rest is honest when it sends you back clearer; escape lies when it leaves the problem untouched and asks for another dose. Check the aftermath before you defend the habit.

exampleSpecs.audience: people checking whether relief actually returns them to life
exampleSpecs.stakes: escape may feel like recovery while leaving the hard task untouched
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The expected proof of recovery fails when the same hard ticket remains untouched.

exampleSpecs.audience: knowledge workers who numb a hard comment
exampleSpecs.stakes: A pleasant screen break can become a way to keep a painful sentence untouched.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist's thoughts expose the difference between a break and a hiding place.

exampleSpecs.audience: people trying to tell rest from disappearance
exampleSpecs.stakes: a soothing activity may become escape if it never returns attention to the problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people use recovery language to test whether a break returns the person to the task.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Two painful paths remain, and only one keeps pleasure from serving as a hiding place.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A genuine two-bad-options choice forces the source's escape warning into a first move.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who hide inside respectable busyness
exampleSpecs.stakes: A respectable activity can become the false cure if it blocks repair.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people talk until the false cure becomes visible without a lecture.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who judge breaks by feeling better
exampleSpecs.stakes: A mood lift can hide a weaker return to duty.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Set up the expected recovery result, then reveal the aftermath tells a different story.
